outline.chapter_title: 1. Foundations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
outline.description: Introduce the scientific and practical motivation for building language models that excel at mathematical reasoning. Covers the history of math benchmarks, key challenges, and the gap between closed‑source powerhouses and open‑source models.
subtopics: Historical development of math reasoning benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K, etc.)
Open‑source vs closed‑source performance landscape
Core difficulties: structured equations, multi‑step logic, tool integration
Evaluation metrics: accuracy, self‑consistency, pass@k, maj@k

outline.description: High‑level view of the entire DeepSeekMath training pipeline from data collection to reinforcement learning. Explains how each phase contributes to final performance.
subtopics: Pre‑training with DeepSeekMath Corpus
Instruction tuning (SFT) with CoT & PoT data
Reinforcement learning using GRPO
Unified training paradigm for SFT/ RL

outline.chapter_title: 3. Constructing a Massive Math Corpus from Common Crawl
subtopics: Seed corpus selection (OpenWebMath) and fastText classifier training
Iterative recall–filter cycle across Common Crawl domains
Deduplication and near‑deduplication techniques
Benchmark decontamination strategy (10‑gram matching)
Statistics: 35.5M pages ➜ 120B tokens, multilingual coverage
Experimental setup: training a 1.3B model on different corpora (MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof‑Pile‑2)
Quality metrics derived from downstream few‑shot math benchmarks
"Higher quality" ⇨ better performance on 8 math benchmarks + MMLU/BBH+code tasks
"Multilingual" benefit → substantial gains in Chinese problem solving
"Large‐scale" advantage → steeper learning curves & longer plateaus
"Base model" initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
"Token distribution": 56% math corpus, 20% GitHub code, 10% natural language, rest other sources
"Training hyperparameters": 500B tokens, lr schedule, batch size 10M tokens
"Results ‑ Math reasoning without tools" (GSM8K, MATH, CMATH etc.) via chain‑of‑thought prompting
"Results ‑ Tool‑enabled solving" via program-of-thought leveraging Python libs (sympy/math)
"Formal mathematics" – autoformalization on miniF2F Isabelle via Sledgehammer integration
"General capability” – MMLU-STEM & BBH improvements; code benchmarks (HumanEval/MBPP) retained

outline.chapter_title: 6. Supervised Fine‑Tuning (SFT) for Mathematical Instruction Data
subtopics: "Data curation process" – English + Chinese problems from GSM8K/MATH/MathInstruct/Lila-OOD/Chinese K‑12 sets; CoT / PoT / Tool–Integrated answers; total 776K examples
"Training protocol" – random concatenation up to 4k tokens; fine‑tune for 500 steps, lr=5e-5, batch=256
"Evaluation setup" – compare against closed/open models with/without tool use on GSM8K/MATH/SAT/COS workshops etc.
"Key findings” – surpasses all open-source 7B plants; closes gap with proprietary GLM-4/Baichuan-3; reaches ~60 % MATH with tool usage

outline.chapter_title: 7. Reinforcement Learning for Math – Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
